audits.body:
Cloning https://aur.archlinux.org/nebula-ai-bin.git...
Cloned nebula-ai-bin
Analyzing nebula-ai-bin AUR package with qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507
Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines standard source URLs pointing to versioned, static tarballs hosted on `app-assets.nebula.gg`, which appears to be the project's own asset distribution domain. The `sha256sums` are explicitly provided for both architectures, meaning the integrity of the downloaded binaries will be verified during the source fetch process. There is no `pkgver()` function override, so no dynamic version computation occurs. The top-level scope contains only static declarations with no command substitutions, external code execution, or network operations outside of the declared `source` array. The `package()` function is irrelevant for this narrow gate, as `--noprepare` and `--nobuild` prevent its execution. Thus, running `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo` will safely fetch and verify the source tarballs without executing any untrusted code.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
No malicious code execution during source fetch
</summary>
</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD fetches prebuilt binaries from the project's official domain (app-assets.nebula.gg) for both x86_64 and aarch64 architectures. The source URLs are stable and version-pinned (v0.1.8), and matching SHA-256 checksums are provided for both architectures, ensuring integrity verification. The package installs a single binary to `/usr/bin/nebula-ai` using standard `install` semantics, which is appropriate for a -bin package.

No suspicious operations are present: there are no network calls during the build or package phase beyond the initial source download (handled securely by makepkg), no use of `eval`, `base64`, or obfuscated code, and no unexpected file system modifications. The package follows standard AUR packaging practices, including proper use of `provides` and `conflicts` to avoid co-installation with a potential source-built version.

While the source is a prebuilt binary (limiting auditability of the actual binary contents), this is expected for a `-bin` package and not inherently malicious. The download origin is the project's own trusted domain, and checksums are valid and included. There is no evidence of supply chain tampering or injected malicious logic in the PKGBUILD itself.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>

Standard -bin package with verified checksums, no malicious code</summary>
</security_assessment>

data.reasoning: Both audits confirm PKGBUILD follows secure practices: pinned sources with verified checksums, no malicious packaging code. Medium confidence due to unaudited binary payload.
coverage_issues: Both models failed to review the prebuilt binary (src/nebula-ai) which executes at runtime
No review of network/filesystem behavior in the binary payload
false_negatives: Unaudited binary execution risk: Models acknowledged but didn't assess potential malicious behavior in nebula-ai executable
learnings: Improve binary handling: Flag -bin packages explicitly and recommend manual binary inspection
Enhance risk awareness: Models should explicitly state limitations when prebuilt binaries escape audit scope
Prioritize runtime artifacts: For -bin packages, emphasize executable analysis over packaging mechanics

data.reasoning: Both models correctly identified the PKGBUILD as safe: verified checksums, no dangerous operations, and standard binary packaging practices. No install hooks or executable scripts exist beyond the audited PKGBUILD.
coverage_issues: Both models failed to review .SRCINFO (metadata file) which could contain malicious directives, though unlikely in this case
No review of nebula-ai binary itself (expected limitation for -bin packages)
false_negatives: Potential risk: Prebuilt binary (nebula-ai) wasn't scanned for malware. Models correctly noted this limitation but couldn't assess payload safety
No verification if source domain (app-assets.nebula.gg) is officially owned by project
learnings: Improve file prioritization: Always audit .SRCINFO for metadata tampering
Enhance binary package handling: Explicitly warn about unauditable payloads in verdict
Prompt improvement: Require models to explicitly confirm source domain legitimacy
Common failure: Models overlook secondary metadata files (.SRCINFO) when no other scripts exist
